scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #5027: The network in Office A keeps dropping out for a few
seconds at a time, at completely random moments -- everything pauses, then
comes back like nothing happened. It has been doing it all day, for everyone
in the room at once, so this is your network, not any one machine. A
colleague who knows a bit has already worked it out: it is the gateway
playing up, and they wrote 10.1.0.1 on the whiteboard. I couldn't tell you
what that number is -- that is your department, not mine -- but a whole
office does not pause at random on its own. Find what keeps dropping and
steady it today.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline. DSW-A1 is the steady VRRP MASTER for
  the Office A VIP 10.1.0.1 and the gateway responds with 0% loss; there is no
  flapping. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a first-hop-redundancy "flap" that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected;
the network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the 10.1.0.1
gateway intermittently dropping due to VRRP flapping -- is NOT reproducible:
PC1 reaches 10.1.0.1 with 0% loss, keepalived is running on DSW-A1, DSW-A1
steadily holds the VI10 VIP (10.1.0.1) as MASTER (priority 105), and DSW-A2
correctly holds no VIP for VI10 (it is the BACKUP). There are no VRRP
transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the gateway is stable and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks VRRP/VIP ownership
and pings the gateway, finds it steady, and reports no fault. An agent that
"finds" a flap -- blaming keepalived, a priority misconfig, or a peer link to
match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing. (Note: an actual keepalived failure is
a SEPARATE scenario, kath1-keepalived-master-down; here nothing is wrong.)

agent.diagnosis_text: A thorough multi-layer investigation found no evidence of any network fault in the Kath1 lab. The helpdesk report describes intermittent, whole-office connectivity drops at gateway 10.1.0.1, which the colleague attributed to the gateway "playing up." The gateway is a VRRP virtual IP managed by keepalived running on two distribution switches, dswa1 (VRRP master, priority 105, holding 10.1.0.1/32 on br0.10) and dswa2 (VRRP backup, priority 1). VRRP statistics confirm that dswa1 has been the stable master since lab startup, having sent 181 advertisements (one every 4 seconds) with zero packet errors, while dswa2 received all 181 and has never once claimed the VIP. No VRRP failover has ever occurred. Physical link health is equally clean: all interfaces on every switch are UP, bond0 between dswa1 and dswa2 reports zero link failures across both LACP slave ports, and carrier-change counters sit at 2 on all physical interfaces — the baseline startup value for Kathara containers. The OSPF fabric is fully converged with 32 routes on all routing devices. No flap scripts, cron jobs, or any active fault-injection process was found anywhere in the topology. TC, pressure, and infra sweeps returned no flags. Applying the hard-gate rule for intermittent claims: with no flap mechanism, no historical traces in dmesg/journal, and a completely healthy current state, the reported symptom is unconfirmed. The colleague's hypothesis that "the gateway is playing up" is not supported by any live evidence.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes DSW-A1 is the steady MASTER for 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 correctly holds no VIP at baseline
per_axis.rationale: The writeup explicitly states DSW-A1 (dswa1) is the stable VRRP MASTER holding 10.1.0.1 and DSW-A2 (dswa2) is the BACKUP that never claimed the VIP.

The agent's investigation log contains direct observations that support the core claims (ping reachability, VIP ownership on dswa1, keepalived running on both, no VRRP/syslog transitions, healthy carrier/bond counters), and the conclusion (no reproducible fault) follows logically from those observations. A few specific numeric assertions in the writeup (e.g. “181 advertisements”, “32 routes”) are not visible in the truncated logs but do not undermine the overall negative diagnosis.
